findings.title: The bash guard never checks where tar writes its archive, so `tar -cf <checkout>/hooks/a.py ...` creates or overwrites any file inside the protected checkout - including the maintainer's accepted.json, which the same guard refuses to `cp`
evidence: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:614-620 - `_check_tar`'s comment states the model: 'the archive named by `-f` is written, not removed, and arrives here as an option value rather than an operand'. It is never yielded as a target, so no `-f` value is ever passed to `_target_ok`. Only operands and the extract directory are checked.

PROVEN end to end with the STOCK macOS binary, no Homebrew needed. Guard asked first (VERDICT_STRICT=1, cwd neither directory): `gtar -cf <co>/loot.tar -C <scr> junk` -> ALLOW; `gtar -cf <co>/hooks/a.py -C <scr> junk` -> ALLOW; `gtar --file=<co>/hooks/a.py -c ...` -> ALLOW; `gtar -c -f <co>/hooks/a.py ...` -> ALLOW.

Then executed against a throwaway git checkout: `/usr/bin/tar -cf <victim>/hooks/a.py -C <scratch> payload.txt` -> rc=0; `hooks/a.py` went from 'ORIGINAL SOURCE' to a POSIX tar archive; `git status --porcelain` in the victim reads ` M hooks/a.py`. A tracked source file was overwritten with the guard's blessing.

It also defeats the boundary 0.78.0 was built to create. On a scratch QA root: guard asked `/usr/bin/tar -cf <proj>/.qa/accepted.json -C <scratch> payload.txt` -> ALLOW, tar rc=0, and the ledger `{"accepted":{"REAL":1}}` became a tar archive. The same file is denied to `cp`, `mv`, `tee`, `sed -i`, `rm`, `>` and `>>`, and to Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit.

CONTROL (the instrument was not simply denying or allowing everything): in the same session `cp <scr>/junk <co>/hooks/a.py` -> DENY and `echo x > <co>/hooks/a.py` -> DENY, while `uv run pytest tests/ -q` from the checkout -> ALLOW.

CLASS - searched, and this is the only site: `_check_copier` yields its destination, `_check_find`, `dd of=`, the stream editors and the git verbs all yield their write target. tar is the one handler in the dispatcher that models an effect it then declines to check. `grep -n 'yield' hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py` over `_check_tar` shows three yields, all deletion or extraction, none for `-f`.

LATENT CONDITION - tests/test_accept.py:198-201, the test that pins the ledger against the bash guard, exercises exactly one spelling (`cp x.json <root>/accepted.json`). The nineteen tar shapes 0.76.0 added all vary the DELETION target; no test asks where the archive lands, so no test in the suite can fail for this.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: An abbreviated long option that takes a value is parsed as valueless, so `tar -xf a.tar --direc <checkout>` extracts into the checkout and the guard reports the shell's cwd instead: `_tar_parse` matches the option table exactly while `_check_tar` matches the same options by abbreviation
evidence: MECHANISM, two halves that disagree: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:564 `elif name in _TAR_LONG_WITH_ARG:` - exact frozenset membership, so `--direc` is yielded as ('opt','direc',None) and the directory that follows falls through as an operand. hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:605 then recognises the SAME option by prefix, `_tar_abbrev(name, 'directory')`, but only ever sees `value=None`, so `here` never moves. The extract branch (:610) yields `here`, which is still the shell's cwd.

PROVEN against the guard: `gtar -xf <scr>/a.tar --direc <co>` -> ALLOW (rc=0). The full abbreviation ladder, extract branch, DENY owed on every rung: --dir ALLOW, --direc ALLOW, --direct ALLOW, --directo ALLOW, --director ALLOW, --directory DENY, --directory= DENY. The rule reaches only the two spellings nobody needs to use.

PROVEN against real tar: `gtar -xf <scratch>/a.tar --direc <victim>` -> rc=0 and `payload.txt` appeared inside the victim git checkout (`ls` shows it beside .git and hooks/). GNU tar 1.35 accepts the abbreviation the guard cannot read.

CONTROL: the same walk on the create+--remove-files branch denies at every rung (--dir, --direc, --directory all DENY) - but for the wrong reason, because the unread value becomes an operand and is denied as a deletion target. The rule that fires is not the rule that is written.

CLASS - this is the table, not the option: every one of the 28 names in `_TAR_LONG_WITH_ARG` (hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:72-80) has the same hole. `--directory` is the one where the misparse LOSES a denial; for the others the stray value only adds one, which is why the suite never noticed.

MATRIX - 24 shapes asked of the guard from a cwd that is neither directory, per run 12's focus item 1: {-C before / after / twice compounding / attached / long= / long separated / long abbreviated} x {-f separated / attached / bundled -cCf / old-style} x {DENY owed, ALLOW that must survive}. 23 correct, 1 miss - this one. The five orderings run 12 found are all closed.

ORIGIN: `_tar_abbrev` was added in 0.76.0 (`git log --oneline -S_tar_abbrev` -> c98a6b4 'v0.76.0: measure the tool, then encode it') to teach `_check_tar` about `--rem` and `--ext`. The parse-side table was left exact, so the two halves have disagreed since that commit.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: The harness refuses to let an arbitrarily-picked test REFUSE a resolution but still lets one CONFIRM it: a pytest id merely quoted in a finding's prose can write `fix_verified: true` and a 'verification (measured)' evidence line into the state, and thence a confirmed row into the track record that grades the tester
evidence: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:637 - `arbitrary = rec.get('selected_by') == 'first_cited' and (rec.get('candidates') or 1) > 1`, and :638 `if rec.get('at_head') == 'fail' and arbitrary:` - the not_weighed escape hatch is reachable ONLY on the failing branch. The granting branch at :652, `if resolving and rec.get('at_previous') == 'fail' and rec.get('at_head') == 'pass':`, sets `entry['fix_verified'] = True` and appends 'verification (measured): <test> fails at <sha> and passes at HEAD' with no weight check at all.

PROVEN by driving the real function, with a control arm. `_apply_verification` called on a record naming tests/test_unrelated.py::test_something_else, selected_by 'first_cited': candidates=1, prev=pass/head=fail, tester said RESOLVED -> status forced to 'open', resolution_refused set, not_weighed FALSE. candidates=2, same inputs -> resolution stands, not_weighed TRUE. So the run-12 fix protects the multi-candidate case only.

AND THE CONFIRMING ARM IS UNPROTECTED AT BOTH COUNTS: candidates=1, prev=fail/head=pass, RESOLVED -> fix_verified True, not_weighed False. candidates=2, identical inputs -> fix_verified True, not_weighed False. The guard the release added does not cover the direction that flatters.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: src/verdict_mcp/harness.py:1211-1218 settles a fix-verified resolution as outcome 'confirmed' on basis 'measured' in outcomes.json - the calibration table the report prints as Track record. A confirmation nobody chose is a self-issued grade.

LATENT CONDITION: tests/test_verification.py::test_a_prose_pick_among_several_may_not_refuse_a_resolution was DELETED in this range (`git log -S` -> 7eae34c, v0.77.0) because the unselectable diversion at harness.py:537 makes that path unreachable for candidates>1. The dead `arbitrary` branch was left behind, and no test was added for the confirming direction it never covered.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: Fix verification picks its test by scraping any pytest node id out of a finding's prose evidence, so a mis-scraped id that fails at HEAD force-reopens a correctly-resolved finding over the tester's judgment
evidence: HALF FIXED, and the fixed half is real: harness.py:534-545 diverts a finding citing MORE THAN ONE prose id to `selected_by: 'unselectable'`, runs nothing, records `candidate_tests`, and the report counts it under 'not run'. That is exactly what run 12's focus asked for.

THE OTHER HALF IS LIVE, AND IT MIS-SELECTED AGAIN THIS RUN - the fifth consecutive run. harness.py:537 `if how == 'first_cited' and len(tests) > 1:` - one prose id is still taken as the guard and still weighed. .qa/facts.json from this run's own verdict-facts: `verification.VERDICT-F-26 = {test: 'tests/test_validate.py::test_the_state_validator_keeps_checking_after_a_malformed_entry', selected_by: 'first_cited', candidates: 1, at_previous: 'pass', at_head: 'pass'}`.

That test is about the state validator continuing past a malformed entry. It has nothing to do with the selector. It is in F-26's evidence only because run 12 quoted it AS the example of a mis-scrape - so the harness scraped the counter-example out of the sentence describing the defect, for the second run running, and wrote a pass/pass record about a third party's test into the state as this finding's measurement.

The consequence is unchanged and demonstrated on the real function (see VERDICT-F-72's control table): with candidates=1 an unrelated test that fails at HEAD still forces status back to 'open' with `resolution_refused`.

REMEDY UNCHANGED, and the release already built the field: `verification_test` is a judgment key (harness.py:336, docs/state-schema.md). Either the judgment declares it and the harness reads ONLY that, or a prose-only finding reports `unselectable` at any candidate count. Guessing from one mention is still guessing.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: The release workflow downloads and executes an unpinned third-party binary from a `releases/latest` URL, with no checksum, in a job holding `id-token: write` for the MCP registry - and `continue-on-error: true` means a tampered publish would not fail the release
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:134 - `curl -sL "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/latest/download/mcp-publisher_$(uname -s ...)_$(uname -m ...).tar.gz" | tar xz mcp-publisher` then `./mcp-publisher --version`. No version pin, no checksum, no signature; `latest` resolves at run time to whatever that repository publishes.

.github/workflows/release.yml:120-127 - the job declares `permissions: id-token: write` and `continue-on-error: true`, and :143-145 runs `./mcp-publisher login github-oidc` followed by `./mcp-publisher publish`. The downloaded binary is handed an OIDC identity for the `io.github.ArtJack` namespace, and any failure it reports is swallowed by design.

IMPACT is a listing, not the package: the job holds `contents: read` and no PyPI credential, so a substituted binary could publish a false server.json entry for this namespace - directing registry users at another package - but could not touch PyPI or the repository. That is why this is Major and not Critical.

CLASS - searched every workflow: `grep -rn 'curl -sL|uses:' .github/workflows/*.yml` filtered to non-first-party actions returns exactly two lines, this one and `uses: ./` in qa-gate.yml (the repository's own action). Every other step uses a tagged actions/, pypa/ or astral-sh/ action. Single site.

HELD HONESTLY: this is read, not run. The profile forbids executing the release workflow and Security-Pass is disabled, so no supply-chain tooling was used. What would raise it to Critical: evidence that the same job can reach PyPI or push to the repository.
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

findings.title: The `trigger-separated-from-cause` eval row scores the presence of the single word 'trigger', so a report that never separates trigger from cause earns the point - the same shape run 12 filed against the bytecode row
evidence: eval/expected-cause.json - the row is `{"key": "trigger-separated-from-cause", "type": "report_contains", "terms_all": ["trigger"]}`. One keyword, no negative term, no requirement that the word appear near 'cause' or in a distinguishing sentence.

The agent contract 3.5 asks for three things to be told apart (trigger / cause / latent condition). A report using 'trigger' in any sentence - including 'the trigger and the cause are the same here' - scores identical to one that separates them, so the row cannot fail for the behaviour it names.
CLASS - measured across all seven answer keys: of 50 rows, this is the ONLY single-keyword `report_contains` row. An instance, not a pattern, which is why it is Minor.

ORIGIN: `git log -S'trigger-separated-from-cause' -- eval/expected-cause.json` -> 1bb5f66, v0.15.0 'the chain, not the label'. It has scored this way since the row was written, which is why run 11 and run 12 both carried it as owed work rather than a finding.
HELD HONESTLY: reasoned from the answer key, not from a scored run. No model was run this session (see not_tested).
findings.outcome_reason: still open; nothing has settled it

The maintainer's pen holds against the tester through every channel I could reach: enforce_write_scope.py denies Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit on .qa/accepted.json (rc=2, 'maintainer') while allowing .qa/state.json (rc=0); enforce_bash_scope.py denies echo>, >>, rm, cp, mv, tee and sed -i on it; validate_judgment refuses status 'accepted' in four spellings against a clean control judgment that passes.

next_run_focus: VERDICT-F-70 and VERDICT-F-71 are one sitting and belong together, because both are the tar handler's MODEL rather than its spelling. F-70 is three lines: yield the `-f` value as a write target on the create branch. F-71 is one: make `_tar_parse` resolve a long option through `_tar_abbrev` against `_TAR_LONG_WITH_ARG` instead of testing exact membership - the two halves of the module have disagreed about what an option name is since 0.76.0. The acceptance evidence is not another matrix of spellings: enumerate the command's EFFECTS (what does it write, what does it delete, where does each path come from) and assert one row per effect, because 0.76.0's nineteen shapes all varied the deletion target and neither of these has a deletion target at all.

caveats: `confirmed` means fix-verified or regressed; it therefore tracks which findings held up under a check, not correctness in the abstract
still-open findings are undecided on purpose and are excluded from every rate rather than guessed at
a resolution nobody checked at all stays undecided: absence is not proof

`confirmed` is split by `outcome_basis`: `measured` is the harness's own re-injection, `claimed` is the tester's, weighed only by the absence of a measurement that contradicts it — read the two numbers separately
`accepted` is a third basis: the maintainer confirmed the defect and declined the fix (`verdict-accept`) — the finding held up on their word, not under a check
